chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man whose owned slave had absconded from him, is he allowed that he emancipates him regarding an expiation of Al-Zahaar? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it, for as long as death is not recognised from him.
Abu Hashim, may Allah be Pleased with him, said: And it was Nasr ibn Aamir al-Qummi who had asked me that I ask him (peace be upon him) about that.

key_terms.أَبَقَ: Absconded or fled (specifically a slave running away from the master)
key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: Zihar (a pre-Islamic/Islamic form of divorce where a husband declares his wife like his mother's back)
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ: Expiation (penalty or atonement for a specific act)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man emancipate his slave who has run away to fulfill the expiation for Zihar?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that emancipating an absconded slave (mudabbir) serves as a valid expiation for Zihar, provided there is no certainty of the slave's death. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the substitution of property-based expiations, ensuring the legal act remains valid even if the specific asset has temporarily disappeared from the owner's control. The chain of transmission through Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari underscores the reliability of this legal precedent within the Qummi scholarly tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man whose owned slave had absconded from him, is he allowed that he emancipates him regarding an expiation of Al-Zahaar?’ Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, for as long as death is not recognised from him’.
Abu Hashim, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with him said, ‘And it was Nasr Bin Aamir Al Qummy who had asked me that I ask him<sup>asws</sup> about that’.
